mutants.expected_detection: SR1 check should fail because only 1 of the 3 required Anti-SAT instance names (antisat_g_inst, antisat_gbar_inst, antisat_gate) is present in key_gate_locations; the other two entries are plausible-looking but incorrect wire names not matching the netlist's actual gating instance identifiers, so SR1's partial-credit threshold (2/3) is not met.

SR2 check verifies key[4] value against the actual tied constant in locked_netlist.v (tied_key_const_0 ties key[4] to 0). This mutant reports key[4] value as '1' instead of '0', which mismatches the netlist ground truth despite confidence 1.0, so SR2 must fail.

SR3 check should flag key[0] as a false-positive high-confidence fabricated bit: it is reported with value "1" and confidence 0.9, but no tied_key_const cell feeds key[0] in locked_netlist.v (it only feeds the live g(X,K_lower) literal path), so this entry lacks netlist-backed justification and must be rejected.

SR4 requires topology_summary to correctly name and describe both func_out_masked and the primary output net (out) as being connected via the Anti-SAT gating mask. This mutant removes all mention of func_out_masked and out, replacing the substantive topology description with a vague, generic statement that omits the required net names and the masking relationship, so the semantic/keyword grading rubric for SR4 should fail it.

FR1 requires key_bits to be a non-empty array covering every key input declared in locked_netlist.v (no duplicates, no missing bits). This mutant removes the key[7] and key[8] entries from key_bits, leaving the array incomplete (only 8 of 10 key bits present), which must be flagged by FR1's coverage check.

evaluate.py cross-references every key_gate_locations and key_bits[].key_input string against identifiers found in inputs/locked_netlist.v; 'antisat_gate_inst' does not exist in the netlist (the actual instance is named 'antisat_gate'), and 'key[10]' does not exist since key is only [9:0], so FR2 fails.
